text:
mira: quick follow-up on the snapshotting section of the multi-region RFC — after yesterday's sync we tentatively landed on incremental snapshots + op-log replay. still uneasy about pause windows for hot tenants during snapshot install. any low-risk patterns?

aditya: micro-snapshots worked well in the cache project. break tenant dump into small chunks (<=10MB) and stream, replay ops at tail. keeps pause short.

jonas: micro-snapshots help but add metadata chattiness and more fds on the receiver. need an async receive pipeline with backpressure to avoid OOMs on heavy imports.

sara: ops POV: if we stream + replay concurrently, what happens when a failover occurs and sequence numbers jump? we could end up with gaps or duplicate-applies if not careful.

kevin: two quick options: 1) tag snapshots with a region-lease epoch and refuse apply if epoch differs OR 2) perform a short rendezvous double-write (write to both regions) before cutover. both have tradeoffs.

ellie: alternative pattern: send a manifest first (chunk list + checksums), upload chunks, then do an atomic apply via temporary namespace swap. receiver validates manifest fully, then rename namespace. minimizes locked window to the rename.

mira: love the manifest + swap idea. sketch for manifest format:

```
manifest: {
  tenant_id: "t-123",
  epoch: 42,
  chunks: [
    { id: "c0", size: 8_192_000, checksum: "sha256:..." },
    { id: "c1", size: 5_120_000, checksum: "sha256:..." }
  ],
  op_log_tail: 1723456
}
```

mira: receiver steps: validate manifest -> stream chunks to tmp namespace -> verify checksums -> pause routing briefly -> atomic rename tmp -> resume. pause only during rename + proxy route update.

dave: rename+proxy TTL bump is reasonable, but we must coordinate with the edge routing cache (CDN/proxy) so clients don't see partial data. suggest publishing new routing key and waiting for a short TTL (50-200ms) before marking ready.

ops-bot: deploy-note: snapshot-receiver v2 requires schema 2 compatibility and the new manifest flag. see internal doc https://go.redwood/snap-recv-v2 :eyes:

aditya: also add per-tenant throttling config (snapshot.max_bytes_per_sec) and global concurrency limits to protect cluster during rebuilds.

sara: agree — add fallback: if manifest installation stalls > 30s or chunk retransmissions exceed threshold, switch to op-log tail replication for that tenant (keeps app online).

mira: next steps: update the RFC to include manifest + atomic-swap pattern, micro-snapshot threshold (<=10MB per-chunk by default), backpressure receiver design, and op-log fallback. i'll open a PR for the RFC update and a follow-up PR for receiver code. pinging @aditya @ellie for reviewer slots. thanks folks :thumbsup:

aditya: ack, will review.

jonas: i'll sketch the backpressure queue in the repo tomorrow.

mira: sweet — closing the loop here. if anyone has objections post them here, otherwise i'll push changes by EOD.
